messages:
anna: Heads-up: CI started failing a bunch of SAST jobs after the nightly rulepack bump. Multiple repos showing the same new finding: `proto-unsafe-serialize` in generated clients.

brad: Repro'd locally. The new rule in rulepack v2026.06.14 flags a pattern in our protos that we intentionally mark safe. Lots of noise.

anna: That's bad timing for the release train. Any way to pin the scanner to previous rulepack while we triage?

tom: We can pin scanner image in the SAST workflow to rulepack v2026.06.07. Quick workaround: update .github/workflows/sast.yml to use `scanner:latest-rulepack-20260607` and re-run. But longer term we need a suppression + review path.

sec-bot: Detected multiple suppression attempts for finding id fp-33021 by `automation-bot` at 2026-06-15T04:12Z. All attempts failed with `403 Forbidden: lacks role sast.suppressionApprover`.

brad: Wait, suppression approvals failed? That's odd, the approvals app worked yesterday.

anna: I just tried to approve one via the web UI and got 403 too. UI shows: `You are not authorized to approve suppressions for this team.`

sec-bot: IAM change note: role `sast.suppressionApprover` membership was altered in org-PR infra-6211 (commit e9f1c). Group dev-frontend@sessions.redwood.com was removed from that role. Audit log points to infra-ci at 2026-06-14T22:30Z.

tom: That explains the 403s. infra change removed a whole approver group during a separate RBAC housekeeping PR. Why wasn't there a pre-merge check for suppression approver membership?

anna: We need two things now: (A) unblock releases with a safe short-term policy, (B) harden the suppression workflow so this doesn't happen silently.

brad: Short-term plan: (1) pin rulepack in CI to the last known-good version across affected repos, (2) issue an ephemeral approver grant to the automation-bot and a named reviewer so pending suppressions can be closed with audit, (3) open rollback PR to restore group binding.

sec-oncall: Authorizing ephemeral approver grant for 30m to `automation-bot@redwood` and `anna@redwood` to clear urgent sup tickets. Audit id GRANT-631a created. Document the grant id in SEC-PR-7001.

anna: Grant received. I'll approve the suppressions that have the needed evidence (diff of generated code + maintainer sign-off). Approving now.

qa-bot: Scan re-run on pinned rulepack shows false positives cleared for 18/20 repos. Two still need manual review.

brad: For durable fixes: (1) suppression approval should require a `trace_id` linking to the scan artifact and a reviewer signature; (2) infra must add a pre-merge CI check that verifies `sast.suppressionApprover` membership for teams touched by the PR; (3) scanner rulepack bumps must be gated by a canary job that runs the new rulepack against a curated corpus of generated code to detect noisy rules.

tom: I'll open infra/PR-6230 to restore the group binding with minimal scope and add the membership pre-merge check. Also adding an action that runs `scannerctl rulepack probe --corpus generated-clients` on rulepack updates.

sec-bot: Created ticket SEC-PR-7001: "rulepack bump caused suppression approver RBAC gap + noisy rule" assigned to tom, priority P1. Link: https://redwood.atlassian/SEC-PR-7001. Audit slice attached: GRANT-631a, infra-6211.

anna: Postmortem items I'm capturing: add rulepack canary, require suppression approvals to include artifact trace_id, add alert when suppression approver role membership changes without a linked ticket in commit message, and update the suppression UI to show required evidence checklist.

brad: Also propose we add a rate-limit on auto-suppressions triggered by automation-bot and require human sign-off for any new rule that flags >5 unique repos in a 12h window.

sec-oncall: Closing Slack incident after approvals finished and CI unblocked. SEC-PR-7001 remains open until PR-6230 merges and the canary pipeline is in place. If suppressions start failing again, ping sec-oncall with GRANT id.

tom: PR-6230 opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/6230  restores group binding + adds membership check + rulepack-canary action. Marked must-pass.

anna: Thanks everyone. Reminder: when bumping shared rulepacks coordinate with the SAST owners channel and schedule a canary run.

brad: Lesson learned: rulepack = platform change. Treat like keystore or other infra-level change and run consumer smoke tests.
